Affectionate nickname for the Leafs, big in headlines and bar talk.
Air Canada Centre, the arena's name until 2018. Plenty of fans still call Scotiabank Arena that.
Maple Leaf Gardens on Carlton Street, the Leafs' home from 1931 to 1999 and the rink of the old Cup teams.

lines.t: Go Leafs Go!
lines.m: The home chant. You'll hear it in bars right across the country.

lines.t: This is the year.
lines.m: What Leafs fans say every autumn, half hoping and half joking.

lines.t: Leafs-Habs on a Saturday night. That's Canada.
lines.m: The oldest rivalry, and the classic Hockey Night in Canada matchup.

lines.t: Kerry Fraser still owes us a Final.
lines.m: In 1993 the referee missed Gretzky's high stick on Doug Gilmour; Gretzky then scored in overtime and LA won the series. Leafs fans never let it go.

lines.t: Four for four against Ottawa. Just saying.
lines.m: Toronto won all four Battle of Ontario playoff series between 2000 and 2004. Pull it out when a Sens fan gets mouthy.

avoid.why: It's always 'Leafs', never 'Leaves'.
Locals swallow the second T. Saying it carefully marks you as a visitor.
Boston fans use it to mock the Leafs' Game 7 collapse in 2013.

memory: Clinching the club's first playoff spot in April 2026, then winning the first NHL playoff game ever played in Utah

lingo.means: The team's rallying cry and hashtag. It came from the fans.
The blue mammoth mascot, unveiled in October 2025.
Utah Hockey Club, the placeholder name for the first season, 2024-25.

lines.t: Tusks up!
lines.m: The rallying cry.

lines.t: Utah Hockey Club for a year, then Mammoth. Good call.
lines.m: The club played 2024-25 under a placeholder name before becoming the Mammoth in 2025.

lines.t: First playoff game in Utah, and we won it. The Delta Center shook.
lines.m: Utah beat Vegas 4-2 at home in April 2026, the first NHL playoff game ever played in the state.

lines.t: Vegas sent us home in 2026. Payback's coming.
lines.m: The Golden Knights won the 2026 first-round series in six games.

avoid.why: Utah took over the Coyotes' players in 2024, but it's a new club and the Coyotes name stayed in Arizona.
The Mammoth name replaced it in 2025.
The name is never plural.

unsure: legends: the club began in 2024 and has no retired greats
rivals: no established rivalry yet; Vegas is listed because of the 2026 playoff series

memory: Towel Power: coach Roger Neilson waving a white towel on a stick in the 1982 playoffs against Chicago, on the way to the club's first Final

lingo.means: Fans waving white towels at playoff games. It began in 1982, after coach Roger Neilson waved one in mock surrender to the referees.
Short for the Canucks. Fans and local media use it all the time.
Fans' word for the Sedin twins' no-look passing magic. Any slick tic-tac-toe passing play can earn the name.
Two fans in green bodysuits who taunted visiting players from beside the penalty box, starting in 2009.

lines.t: Towel Power!
lines.m: The playoff rallying cry. Grab a white towel and wave it.

lines.t: McLean's save on Reichel, then Bure in double OT. Best night ever.
lines.m: Game 7 in Calgary, 1994: a sprawling overtime save, then Pavel Bure's winner. Canucks fans never tire of it.

lines.t: LaFayette hit the post. I can still hear it.
lines.m: Game 7 of the 1994 Final in New York: a late Canucks shot rang off the post with Vancouver down a goal.

lines.t: Leafs in town, so it's a four o'clock puck drop. Typical.
lines.m: Saturday games against Toronto often start early to suit TV viewers back East. Canucks fans call it Toronto bias.

lines.t: Bring back the Green Men.
lines.m: Fond nostalgia for the penalty-box pranksters of the 2011-era teams.

avoid.say: The Canucks have won a Cup, right?
avoid.why: They reached the Final in 1982, 1994 and 2011 and lost all three.
Losing Game 7 of the Final at home to the Bruins still hurts.

memory: Winning the 2023 Stanley Cup in their sixth season, after reaching the Final in their very first year

lingo.means: T-Mobile Arena, the Knights' home ice.
The team's motto: a club built from scratch in Las Vegas.
The Gila monster mascot.
The home chant.

lines.t: Welcome to the Fortress!
lines.m: The home greeting.

lines.t: Final in year one, Cup in year six.
lines.m: The fastest rise of any expansion team.

lines.t: Go Knights Go!
lines.m: The home chant.

lines.t: Get there early for the pregame show.
lines.m: The Knights' theatrical pregame show is famous.

lines.t: Flower was our first hero.
lines.m: Goalie Marc-André Fleury starred in the early seasons.

avoid.why: The official name is just Vegas.
They made the Final in year one and won the Cup in 2023.

unsure: rivals: no clear consensus; Kings, Sharks and Oilers are all cited
legends: young club; only Fleury is a clear great

memory: Winning the franchise's first Stanley Cup in 2018, clinched in Las Vegas

lingo.means: The call for fans to wear red at home games.
Fan and team slogan, a play on the nickname.
Nickname from the Verizon Center days, still heard for the arena.

lines.t: Let's go Caps!
lines.m: The home chant.

lines.t: Rock the red.
lines.m: Wear red to the game.

lines.t: 2018 was worth the wait.
lines.m: The first Cup after decades of near misses.

lines.t: Pens week. I'm already nervous.
lines.m: Pittsburgh knocked the Caps out of the playoffs many times.

lines.t: I still call it the Phone Booth.
lines.m: Fond use of the old arena nickname.

avoid.why: The arena was renamed in 2017.
Years of playoff losses to Pittsburgh made them the Caps' great rival.

unsure: legends: Alex Ovechkin left out; he is playing his announced final season in 2026-27

memory: The NHL returning to Winnipeg in 2011, 15 years after the original Jets left for Phoenix

lingo.means: Fans dress head to toe in white for home playoff games, with street parties outside the rink. It began in 1987 as Winnipeg's answer to Calgary's C of Red.
Fans shout it during O Canada at home games, a nod to the anthem and to the team's owners, True North Sports & Entertainment. It started in 2011.
Locals' joking name for the city and its brutal winters.
Winnipeg's famous windy downtown corner. Fans packed it to celebrate when the NHL came back in 2011.

lines.t: Whiteout's on. Wear white.
lines.m: The playoff dress code. Turn up in colour and you'll stick out.

lines.t: Calgary had the C of Red, so we gave them a Whiteout.
lines.m: Fans love that the tradition started in 1987 as a reply to Flames fans.

lines.t: Fifteen years without a team. Never again.
lines.m: The original Jets left in 1996 and the NHL only came back in 2011. Fans don't take it for granted.

lines.t: Teemu's 76 as a rookie. Nobody's touching that.
lines.m: Teemu Selanne scored 76 goals for the original Jets in 1992-93, still the NHL rookie record.

lines.t: Gretzky's Oilers wrecked every spring back then.
lines.m: Edmonton knocked the original Jets out of the playoffs six times between 1983 and 1990. Older fans still grumble about it.

avoid.say: The Jets came back from Phoenix
avoid.why: Today's Jets were the Atlanta Thrashers; the original Jets became the Coyotes.

avoid.say: That rink's too small for the NHL
avoid.why: Canada Life Centre is the league's smallest arena, and locals are proud of how loud it gets.

unsure: rivals: no settled modern rival; the Oilers (1980s playoffs), Wild (division) and Flames are all cited
